# redfish_power_restore_policy (Resource)

What the host does when AC power returns after a loss (Redfish ComputerSystem.PowerRestorePolicy), written to the BMC and effective at the next AC power loss, without a reboot. Manage it in one place only: the BIOS attribute "Restore AC Power Loss" (ACPLBMC000) is pushed to the BMC by the BIOS at every boot unless it is "No change", and would overwrite this value. Destroy only removes the resource from state.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Takes effect at the next AC power loss, no reboot needed. Keep the BIOS setting
# "Restore AC Power Loss" at "No change", or the BIOS overwrites this at every boot.
resource "redfish_power_restore_policy" "board" {
  redfish_server { redfish_alias = "bmc" }
  policy = "LastState"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `policy` (String) AlwaysOn, AlwaysOff or LastState.

### Optional

- `redfish_server` (Block List) List of server BMCs and their respective user credentials (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--redfish_server))
- `system_id` (String) System ID; defaults to the first system.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Redfish URI of the computer system.

<a id="nestedblock--redfish_server"></a>
### Nested Schema for `redfish_server`

Optional:

- `endpoint` (String) Server BMC IP address or hostname
- `password` (String, Sensitive) User password for login
- `redfish_alias` (String) Alias name for server BMCs. The key in provider's `redfish_servers` map
- `ssl_insecure` (Boolean) This field indicates whether the SSL/TLS certificate must be verified or not
- `user` (String) User name for login
